score.name: Ryan Specialty Holdings, Inc.
score.sector: Finance / Insurance brokerage & underwriting management (wholesale broker, binding authority, MGU) — SIC 6411
score.moat_justification: A moderate moat (5/10): a scaled specialty-insurance distribution platform — wholesale brokerage, binding authority and delegated-authority MGUs — whose carrier appointments, placement volume and E&S product breadth (300+ products) take years to replicate, and which converts revenue to owner's earnings at a 16-19% margin with almost no physical capex. It is not wider: the producing asset walks out the door, rivals (Amwins, CRC) hold comparable scale, and the ROIC record no longer supports a strong-moat claim — roic_proxy fell from 18.0% in FY2022 to 9.4% in FY2025 (fundamentals.json) as debt-funded acquisitions ($1,708,737,000 of business combinations in FY2024, $746,485,000 in FY2025) were done at full prices, while operating margin stayed in a 16.5-17.7% band. A moat of 7+ would need ROIC sustainably well above the cost of capital; Ryan's measured history is heading the other way.

overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:shares — no diluted share count is carried in EDGAR companyfacts for any fiscal year (shares_diluted blank in financials_history.csv), so the engine emits no tier. The GAAP Class A diluted count in the 10-K EPS note (138,246,414 for FY2025) is NOT the right denominator for consolidated owner's earnings: Ryan is an Up-C — consolidated OCF/capex/SBC cover 100% of Ryan Specialty, LLC including the noncontrolling interest, while the GAAP diluted count excludes the 135,429,254 exchangeable LLC Common Units as antidilutive for FY2025 (they were dilutive and included in several 2025 quarters, e.g. Q3 2025 diluted 273,462k — the GAAP denominator flips with the antidilution test and cannot divide a consolidated numerator). The company's own adjusted diluted share count (279,029k for FY2025) is the total-economic-share denominator built for exactly this perimeter: Class A diluted + all LLC Common Units as exchanged + unvested award dilution. The engine applies this single FY2025 value to every missing year; FY2024's own adjusted count in the same release is 276,288k, so FY2024 OE/share is understated ~1.0% and FY2023 by a similar small amount — disclosed, small, and in the conservative direction for the median base year. The same value is the TTM denominator in ttm.json (H1 2026's own adjusted count was 270,080k after Q2 2026 buybacks, so the TTM base is ~3% conservative).

description.text: Founded by Patrick G. Ryan in 2010, Ryan Specialty is an international specialty insurance intermediary that provides specialty products, solutions, and services for insurance brokers, agents, and carriers. We provide distribution, underwriting, product development, administration, and risk management services through our wholesale brokerage platform and, on behalf of insurance carriers, through delegated underwriting authority via our managing underwriter, binding authority, and national program operations. Our expertise spans an extensive array of property, casualty, professional lines, transportation, personal lines, workers’ compensation, and employee benefits insurance. Our mission is to provide industry-leading innovative solutions for insurance brokers, agents, and carriers. For retail insurance brokers, we assist in the placement of complex or otherwise hard-to-place risks. For insurance carriers, we work with retail and wholesale insurance brokers to source, onboard, underwrite, and service these same types of risks. A significant majority of the premiums we place are bound in the E&S market, which includes Lloyd’s of London, which we refer to as Lloyd’s. There is often significantly more flexibility in terms, conditions, and rates in the E&S market relative to the Admitted or “standard” insurance market.

about.description_short: Founded in 2010, Ryan Specialty (NYSE: RYAN) is a service provider of specialty products and solutions for insurance brokers, agents, and carriers. Ryan Specialty provides distribution, underwriting, product development, administration, and risk management services by acting as a wholesale broker and a managing underwriter with delegated authority from insurance carriers. Our mission is to provide industry-leading innovative specialty insurance solutions for insurance brokers, agents, and carriers. Learn more at ryanspecialty.com.

# RYAN — Ryan Specialty Holdings, Inc.

NYSE: RYAN · Finance / Insurance brokerage & underwriting management (SIC 6411) · Price $41.91 · Market cap $11,694,105,390 (dcf_numbers.json)

## What it is

A specialty-insurance distribution platform, founded 2010 and IPO'd in 2021 in an Up-C structure: the public company is sole managing member of Ryan Specialty, LLC and owned 49.1% of the LLC Common Units at December 31, 2025 (Form 10-K, Note 1); the rest is held by noncontrolling LLC unitholders whose units are exchangeable 1-for-1 into Class A stock (paired with Class B shares). It operates three channels — Wholesale Brokerage, Binding Authority and Underwriting Management (MGUs/program administrators with delegated authority) — across commercial, industrial, institutional, governmental and personal lines, and, in the 10-K's own words, "with the exception of the Company's equity method investments, the Company does not take on any underwriting risk": carriers keep the risk, Ryan keeps commissions and fees. FY2025 revenue was $2,994,582,000 (+21.9% YoY, financials_history.csv). The growth engine has been acquisitions: business combinations consumed $446,682,000 (FY2023), $1,708,737,000 (FY2024) and $746,485,000 (FY2025) of investing cash (10-K Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows), funded with the Term Loan B, the 2030/2032 senior secured notes and the revolver. The 2026 prints show the model downshifting: Q2 2026 total revenue grew 7.2% YoY to $916.6 million on 6.7% organic growth, Adjusted EBITDAC was $326.9 million at a 35.7% margin and adjusted diluted EPS $0.74 (Q2 2026 earnings release); management guides FY2026 organic growth to mid-single digits (toward the upper end), the CFO said a meaningful acquisition is unlikely to close in 2026, and the multi-year Empower restructuring programme absorbed $39.3 million of costs in H1 2026. Capital returns stepped up instead: ~8.1 million shares repurchased for $260 million in Q2 2026 and the buyback authorization raised by $300 million, with company-reported net leverage ~3.3x at quarter-end.

## Owner's earnings

- **Conservative OE (OCF − capex − SBC), FY2025:** OCF $643,667,000 − capex $70,967,000 − SBC $69,451,000 = **$503,249,000** (financials_history.csv; dcf_numbers.json base OE total latest FY). Capex ties to the 10-K cash-flow statement line by line: capital expenditures $67,953,000 + asset acquisitions $3,014,000 = $70,967,000 (FY2024: $47,001,000 = $47,001,000; FY2023: $29,776,000 = $29,776,000). One enrichment caveat: fundamentals.json's OE block is not used anywhere in this analysis — its capex leg reads only PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets (its own tags_used lists that single tag), so it shows FY2025 capex of $3,014,000 and OE of $571,202,000 (a 19.1% OE margin) against the scored chain's $70,967,000 / $503,249,000 (16.8%); every OE margin quoted below is computed on the scored chain in financials_history.csv. OE was positive in 4 of the last 5 fiscal years — the exception is FY2021 (−$165,902,000), when capex spiked to $352,939,000, of which $343,158,000 was a single PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets fact (capex_provenance) around the IPO-era reorganisation; it is outside the base window.
- **Maintenance OE (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC):** $41,401,000 for FY2025 (financials_history.csv). Not usable here: the CSV's net-income leg ($63,399,000) is net income *attributable to Ryan Specialty Holdings, Inc.* only — consolidated net income was $214,157,000 with $150,758,000 attributable to noncontrolling interests (10-K EPS note) — and the D&A leg is depreciation only ($13,089,000), excluding the $274,426,000 of acquired-intangible amortisation. It mixes an attributable numerator with consolidated cash flows, so it collapses mechanically. Not used as the base.
- **Per-share figures require the Up-C correction — see OVERRIDE.** On the corrected total-economic-share denominator (279,029,000 shares, by override): FY2023 OE/share $1.3536, FY2024 $1.3937, FY2025 $1.8036 in engine terms (dcf_numbers.json prints base OE latest per share $1.8035723885330917 and the normalised (median) figure $1.3936615907307126).
- **TTM base — built and USED.** ttm.py legs (ttm.json, through 2026-06-30): OCF FY $643,667,000 − prior YTD $210,760,000 + current YTD $125,618,000 = TTM $558,525,000; capex FY $70,967,000 − $37,210,000 + $31,988,000 = TTM $65,745,000; SBC FY $69,451,000 − $39,798,000 + $38,740,000 = TTM $68,393,000. **TTM OE total $424,387,000 → $1.5209422676495992/share** on the override denominator. The TTM total is below FY2025's $503,249,000 because H1 2026 OCF ($125,618,000) ran well below H1 2025 ($210,760,000) despite higher revenue — H1 cash timing plus Empower cash costs; the TTM base ($1.5209) sits between the normalised median ($1.3937) and the latest FY ($1.8036), which is the right place for a decelerating, seasonally H2-weighted broker. **Base used = TTM $1.5209/share** (base_source: ttm_json).
- Balance sheet at FY2025 (financials_history.csv): cash $158,322,000, debt current $60,187,000 + long-term $3,291,462,000, engine net debt $3,193,327,000; lease liabilities a further $179,076,000. Not in the engine's net debt: expected Tax Receivable Agreement payments of $459.0 million in aggregate and accrued contingent consideration of $148,388,000 (10-K) — real claims on the same cash flow.

## OVERRIDE — shares (filing; the Up-C denominator)

- **The gap:** EDGAR companyfacts carries no diluted share fact for this filer in any year (`shares_diluted` blank for FY2019–FY2025), so the preliminary run exited DATA_GAP:shares with no tier.
- **Why the obvious fix is wrong:** the 10-K EPS note's GAAP diluted count — 138,246,414 for FY2025 (Note 11) — divides *attributable* earnings. It excludes the 135,429,254 LLC Common Units the same note lists as antidilutive for FY2025, even though consolidated OCF/capex/SBC cover 100% of the LLC including those unitholders' share. The GAAP denominator also flips with the antidilution test quarter to quarter (Q3 2025 diluted was 273,462k with the units included; the nine-month figure was 138,090k with them excluded). Dividing consolidated OE by 138.2M would roughly double OE/share and print a fake tier — the VNOM/Up-C failure shape, caught here before it shipped.
- **The decision:** `shares_override = 279,029,000, kind "filing"` — the company's own FY2025 *adjusted* diluted share count from its Q4 2025 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1 to Form 8-K, 2026-02-12): Class A diluted 138,246k + impact of all LLC Common Units exchanged 135,429k + dilutive impact of unvested equity awards 5,354k = 279,029k. Cross-checks: the 10-K cover page shows 264,189,701 shares outstanding at February 9, 2026 (Class A 129,680,816 + Class B 134,508,885 — basic total-economic shares, before award dilution), and FY2024's adjusted count in the same release is 276,288k.
- **Known approximations, disclosed:** the engine applies the single FY2025 value to every missing year, so FY2024 OE/share is understated ~1.0% against its own 276,288k count (conservative for the median) and FY2023 by a similar small amount; the TTM denominator likewise uses 279,029,000 where H1 2026's own adjusted count was 270,080k after Q2 2026 buybacks (~3% conservative). The override is flagged OVERRIDE_OUT_OF_BAND by construction — there is no filed value to anchor the 0.1x–10x band (last_filed_value is null) — and judgment.json carries the ack_reason saying exactly that; make_score's measured impact is in the registry (the override unblocks the tier: without it there is no score at all).

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow

Justification: a scaled specialty-insurance distribution platform — wholesale brokerage, binding authority and delegated-authority MGUs — whose carrier appointments, placement volume and E&S product breadth (300+ specialty products, Q2 2026 call) take years to replicate, converting revenue to owner's earnings at a 16–19% margin on almost no physical capex. It is not wider: the producing asset walks out the door, rivals hold comparable scale, and the ROIC record no longer supports a strong-moat claim (below).

- FOR: scale — FY2025 revenue $2,994,582,000 across the three channels, one of the largest US specialty distribution platforms; delegated underwriting authority granted by carriers on loss-ratio track records and programme data, earned over years; structural E&S tailwind as complexity pushes risks out of the admitted market into the channels Ryan serves; asset-light cash conversion (conservative OE margin 18.6% of revenue FY2023, 15.8% FY2024, 16.8% FY2025, financials_history.csv).
- AGAINST: a people business — producers are portable, customers not contractually locked in, Amwins/CRC and carrier-direct channels compete for the same flow; **ROIC falling — roic_proxy 18.0% (FY2022), 17.3% (FY2023), 10.7% (FY2024), 9.4% (FY2025) (fundamentals.json), with operating margin flat in a 16.5–17.7% band and no filed gross-profit line (revenue is net commissions/fees): growth is being bought at rising prices, not earned on cheap capital** — a moat of 7+ would need ROIC sustainably well above the cost of capital, and Ryan's measured history heads the other way; leverage (net debt 7.5x the TTM OE total, plus TRA and contingent-consideration claims); E&S cycle softening (property pricing declines, builders-risk weakness, new capacity) already visible in the prints; Up-C claims ahead of Class A holders ($64,126,000 of tax distributions to noncontrolling unitholders and $25,169,000 of TRA payments in FY2025 alone, 10-K cash-flow statement).
- Fade: CAP = clamp(2 + 1.3 × 5, 2, 15) = **8.5 years**; growth holds 2 years, then converges to the 2.5% terminal rate.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-20)

Engine release 5.5.0, price $41.91, base = TTM $1.5209422676495992/share (--ttm), moat 5.

**Growth-start sanity check (the reason for the offsets):** the engine's blended start is 21.22% (revenue CAGR 5y 24.08%, 3y 20.49%, latest revenue YoY 21.95%, OE/share CAGR 15.42% — dcf_numbers.json growth_components). Every component straddles the debt-funded acquisition spree (business combinations of $1,708,737,000 in FY2024 and $746,485,000 in FY2025), so the blend measures consolidation, not a run rate. The clean prints: Q1 2026 organic growth 10.1%, Q2 2026 total revenue +7.2% YoY with organic +6.7%, FY2026 organic guidance at mid-single digits toward the upper end, and management stating meaningful M&A is unlikely to close in 2026. Scenario starts were therefore set directly (offsets −0.2522/−0.1822/−0.1322/−0.0822/−0.0322 against the blend): **−4% / +3% / +8% / +13% / +18%**. The super-bull start (18%) sits below FY2025's actual revenue print (+21.9%) with this written reason: that print was acquisition-funded, the guided organic rate is mid-single-digit, and even the bull cases must now be earned organically or from a 2027 M&A restart. Probabilities shifted bearish versus the 10/25/30/25/10 default to **15/25/30/20/10** for the deceleration, the guided margin pressure and the leverage; OE multipliers stay at the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25, which is where Empower costs, E&S pricing and interest expense bite.

| Scenario | Prob | g start | OE mult | IV@15% | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −4.0% | 0.75 | $7.13 | 4.46% |
| Bear | 25% | 3.0% | 0.90 | $11.46 | 5.93% |
| Base | 30% | 8.0% | 1.00 | $15.66 | 7.37% |
| Bull | 20% | 13.0% | 1.10 | $21.16 | 9.16% |
| Super bull | 10% | 18.0% | 1.25 | $29.47 | 11.66% |
| **Weighted** | | | | **$15.81** | **7.45%** |

Weighted IV@20% $11.02, IV@25% $8.40; upside at the 15% hurdle −62.27% (dcf_numbers.json). Diagnostics: OE yield 3.63%, terminal value 19.5% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.14x, net debt / normalized OE 7.52x. **Tier by numbers: D** — and four of the five scenarios are individually D; only the super bull (11.66%) reaches the C band, still below the hurdle: at $41.91 there is no modelled path to Andrew's 15% hurdle.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved

- **DATA_GAP:shares (preliminary run):** resolved by the filing-sourced shares_override above (279,029,000 total-economic adjusted diluted shares); data_gap_uncovered is empty in the final run.
- **STALE_FY:** FY2025 ended ~10 months before the run. ttm.py was run and the TTM base used (--ttm); legs quoted in Owner's earnings above. TTM OE/share $1.5209 vs latest-FY $1.8036 and normalised $1.3937 — the TTM is the freshest and the middle of the three, not an outlier.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE:** explained from the FY2025 cash-flow statement itself (10-K). Consolidated net income was $214,157,000 (the CSV's $63,399,000 leg is the attributable slice); the gap to OCF of $643,667,000 is non-cash addbacks, led by amortisation of acquired intangibles $274,426,000, plus equity-based compensation $69,451,000, prepaid/deferred compensation $38,779,000, deferred income taxes $26,047,000 and a further $48,597,000 of deferred tax expense from common-control reorganisations, and depreciation $13,089,000, partly offset by equity-method income of $21,236,000 and a commissions-receivable build of $57,559,000. The same pattern (amortisation $157,845,000 in FY2024, $106,799,000 in FY2023, rising with each acquisition) repeats in 2023–2025 — it is the roll-up's accounting shadow, not a one-off inflating OCF. Note the flip side: that amortisation is the income-statement echo of the $746M–$1.7B/yr of business combinations the OE definition does not charge as capex (see Thoughts).
- **SBC_TAG_RECONCILED:** FY2021 only — AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $86,456,000 exceeded ShareBasedCompensation $67,534,000 by 28.0% and the Allocated figure was used. FY2022–FY2025 and every TTM leg use ShareBasedCompensation unreconciled (ttm.json sbc_reconciled_legs is empty), so the reconciliation does not touch the scored base; it is recorded here as required.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH:** SIC 6411 (insurance agents/brokers) trips the Finance-sector flag, and confidence is graded low as the rule requires. On substance the fit is better than for a risk-bearing insurer: Ryan takes no underwriting risk, premium cash held in a fiduciary capacity ($1,426,148,000 at FY2025) is excluded from the engine's cash figure and its net change ($237,616,000 in FY2025) runs through financing, not OCF — so the OE numerator is commission cash flow, not policyholder float. Following the sweep's broker precedent (BRO, WTW: no notch), there is **no tier_override**; the misfit is carried as low confidence, not a notch.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:shares:** see OVERRIDE — the override fills a total filing gap (it replaces no filed value), is filing-sourced, and its construction and approximations are disclosed there and in judgment.json.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD:** super-bull IV@15% is 4.14x super-bear. Confidence is low, and the verdict is sized to the conservative end — moot for direction here, since even the super-bull IRR (11.66%) reaches only the C band, below the 15% hurdle.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT:** net debt $3,193,327,000 is 7.52x normalized OE (key_numbers.md), before $179,076,000 of lease liabilities, $459.0 million of expected TRA payments and $148,388,000 of accrued contingent consideration (10-K). The company's own ~3.3x net-leverage figure (Q2 2026) is measured against Adjusted EBITDAC, a far larger denominator than owner's earnings. The bear cases carry the stress: 40% combined weight on bear/super-bear with OE multipliers of 0.90/0.75 — levered OE is exactly what those cases haircut.

## My thoughts / overlay

- **The method range is C→D, and the swing factor is growth, not the base.** The preliminary run on the normalised base ($1.3937) with the engine's unadjusted 21.2% blend and default probabilities printed a weighted IRR of 10.89% and IV@15% of $26.23 (Tier C). The final run uses a *higher* base (TTM $1.5209) yet prints 7.45% / $15.81 (Tier D), because the scenario starts were recalibrated to what the company is actually printing and guiding (single-digit organic) instead of its acquisition-era CAGR. Anyone quoting a single RYAN number without its growth basis is hiding the ball; on no defensible basis does it clear 15% at $41.91.
- **The OE definition is generous to a roll-up, and the verdict is D anyway.** Owner's earnings charge only $70,967,000 of physical capex; the $746,485,000 of FY2025 business combinations (and the $274,426,000/yr of resulting intangible amortisation) are treated as growth investment outside the base. For a broker whose growth model *is* buying books of business, a maintenance-capex view that charged even part of acquisition spend would cut the base hard — the falling ROIC (18.0% → 9.4%) is that cost showing up in another column. The D here is printed on the kind definition; the unkind one is worse.
- What is genuinely good: a scaled, diversified specialty platform with a structural E&S tailwind, a 16.8% FY2025 OE margin, a buyback now retiring stock ($260 million in Q2 2026), and a restructuring programme aimed at the cost base. None of that is the debate — the debate is price: at $41.91 the market capitalises this as if the acquisition-era growth were organic and permanent.
- Hurdle math: the stock clears Andrew's 15% hurdle at the weighted IV@15% of **$15.81** — 62% below the $41.91 price; even the base-case IV@15% ($15.66) and the bull-case IV@15% ($21.16) sit far below it.

## Final verdict

- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 7.45% on the TTM base; tier by numbers D, no tier override, bear and bull cases also D)
- Confidence: **low** (sector model misfit, wide scenario spread, high leverage, and a share denominator that rests on a filing-sourced override for a total EDGAR gap)
- One-liner: Scaled specialty-insurance distribution platform, moat 5/10 — but its growth was bought with debt-funded acquisitions and has decelerated to single digits: on the TTM base of $1.52/share the weighted IRR is 7.45% (Tier D) at $41.91 with weighted IV@15% $15.81; it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$15.81, and even the super-bull case (11.66% IRR) does not clear 15% at this price.
